title: The Impact of Device Use on Our Children
text_original: households (3:48 vs. 1:52 hours daily). Our report aims to help you understand these shifts and navigate them thoughtfully. How we respond to these changes today will shape not just our children's relationship with technology, but their development, learning, and well-being for years to come. We invite you to explore the full report and our corresponding Parents' Ultimate Guides that give practical "device advice" for kids of all ages. Together, we can build a healthier digital future for our children. James P. Steyer Founder and CEO Common Sense Media Advisers: Fashina Aladé Heather Kirkorian Survey development Supreet Mann and design: Angela Calvin Data collection: Ipsos U.S. Public Affairs Survey translation: Julia Valdivia Data analysis and Angela Calvin interpretation: Supreet Mann Report writing: Supreet Mann Designers: Amy Buller Copy editors: Christopher Dare Communications: Christian Medina Beltz Kirsten Olsen Cahill Edda Collins Coleman The report authors and project team express their gratitude to the parents who gave their time to take the survey. We also wish to acknowledge the work of Vicky Rideout for her contributions to the development of the Common Sense Census reports over the past waves of data collection. Additionally, we thank the following individuals for their time and expertise reviewing the survey and providing feedback: Claire Bessant, Jessica Blacksten, Lin Ong, and Kalia Vogelman-Natan. Suggested citation: Mann, S., Calvin, A., Lenhart, A., and Robb, M.B. (2025). The Common Sense census: Media use by kids zero to eight, 2025. San Francisco, CA: Common Sense Media. Key Findings. . .
text_simplified: This report aims to help parents understand and appropriately assess the changes in device usage, which will affect their children’s growth, development, and psychological and physical well-being.

review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'health' (صحة), while the English uses 'well-being', which is broader and not an exact equivalent; this slightly shifts the meaning.
